alignments.note: Quantifier to the determiner it writes.
δόσις rendered by the first *gift*; split from its adjective under rule 26.
Attributive adjective; reordered before the noun, permitted by rule 15.
Coordinating conjunction.
Second quantifier.
δώρημα rendered by the second *gift*.
Attributive adjective.

The adverb's own English gloss is *from above*; *from* spells the -θεν source suffix rather than answering to any Greek preposition, so it rides with the adverb and rule 17 heads the unit on *above*, the meaning-bearing word. Heading on *from* would rest only on its standing first, which rule 17 refuses, and rule 71 makes the same choice against an initial *in*, *on* or *at*.
Finite copula, expressed in the Greek and written by the ASV.
Participle rendered by the phrasal *coming down*; head on the participial word, since *coming* glosses the lexeme rather than being an empty support verb of the kind rule 91 sends to its complement.
Preposition to the English preposition governing the phrase, rule 36.
Article to *the*, rule 19; the ASV writes no case preposition here, ἀπό having taken *from*.
Head noun stands bare behind its own article.
The ASV gives *lights* no determiner, so this article has no *the* to anchor: rule 23, with rule 21 forbidding a bare *of* on it.
Genitive noun rendered *of lights*; the case preposition stays with the determinerless noun under rule 21, headed on the noun under rule 17.
Preposition to *with*. The ASV writes *with whom* as two words, so rule 35's portmanteau case does not arise and the pair splits under rule 2.
Relative pronoun to *whom*.

The clause's single English negation is the determiner *no*, and παραλλαγή is a plain lexical noun with no negation of its own, so rules 41 and 59 do not empty the negator: it keeps the negating word. The competing reading joins οὐκ and παραλλαγή into one unit on *no variation* under rule 39's test; I took the split because *variation* answers to the noun independently and *no* answers to the negator, so nothing is fused. Rule 87 is not in question, the verse's πᾶς tokens standing in the previous clause.

`ἔνι` rendered by *can be*; the supplied modal is a rule 7/9 helper and rule 17 heads the unit on the lexical *be* rather than the auxiliary. Nothing else in the clause can carry the modal — `παραλλαγή` is a plain noun, `οὐκ` a negator, `παρ᾽ ᾧ` a prepositional phrase — so no hedge is owed and rules 84 and 91 warn against one where nothing competes. That is what distinguishes this from JAS.1.13, where the privative `ἀπείραστος` carries the modal in its own morphology and the expressed `ἐστίν` is left only *be*: there a source word licenses the *cannot*, here none does. `ἔνειμι` is unattested in the corpus, but the corpus aligns *can* to a finite verb in every one of its eighteen units.
Predicate noun on its own English word.
The disjunctive under negation is rendered *neither*; the word answers to the conjunction, so it is aligned rather than read as part of the negation, which οὐκ has already taken in *no*.
Genitive noun rendered *by turning*; determinerless, so the case preposition rides with the noun under rule 21 and heads on it under rule 17, exactly as this verse's own τῶν φώτων → *of lights* does.

The ASV expands the noun into *shadow that is cast*; the supplied relativizer, copula and participle are rule 7 helpers on the noun, which is what the clause is predicated of and the only token in the phrase able to carry them — rules 53 and 92's test of what is left in the phrase, there being no article here for rule 31's carve-out to reach. Rule 66 heads on *shadow*, the word that glosses ἀποσκίασμα. The materially different reading takes *that is cast by* as an expanded realization of the genitive case and puts the whole of it on τροπῆς under rule 67's noun-carrier arm, leaving *shadow* alone; I did not take it, because rule 67's frames are prepositional (*by reason of*, *in the matter of*) and a supplied finite relative clause is not one, and because the casting is predicated of the shadow rather than of the turning.

review_notes: Reviewed and returned with one note changed and no unit boundaries or heads altered.
All 23 source and 30 target ids partitioned exactly once; every aligned unit has nonempty arrays with both heads inside them.
s014 τῶν is the verse's only unrepresented unit; a reference comparison may report it as a disagreement, and under rules 21 and 23 that is not a correction.

Contested unit 1 — s018 οὐκ → *no*, taken as a split against the competing joined reading on *no variation*. Rules 41 and 59 empty a negator only where the second word is itself a negative able to carry the English negation alone; παραλλαγή is a plain lexical noun with its own English word, so nothing licenses emptying and rule 2 keeps the pair apart. Stated in the unit's note.

Contested unit 2 — s023 ἀποσκίασμα → *shadow that is cast*, with *by* left on τροπῆς. The accepted alignment made this call correctly but did not name the alternative, which rule 16 requires; I added it to the unit's note. The alternative would give *that is cast by turning* whole to τροπῆς headed on *turning* and leave *shadow* bare, reading the supplied clause as an expanded case frame under rule 67. Rule 67's frames are prepositional, and the casting is predicated of the shadow, so the accepted reading stands.

Verse-internal consistency check under rule 24: both determinerless genitives are analysed alike — φώτων → *of lights* and τροπῆς → *by turning* each keep the supplied case preposition on the noun under rule 21, while the articular ἀπὸ τοῦ πατρός splits three ways under rule 13 with a bare *the* on the article.

Head checks under rule 17: *above* over *from* for ἄνωθεν (rule 71's refusal of an initial preposition), *be* over *can* for ἔνι (rule 9), *lights* and *turning* over their case prepositions, *coming* for καταβαίνω since the verb glosses the lexeme rather than supporting it (rule 91), and *shadow* for ἀποσκίασμα (rule 66).
